ElementDescription: Q6 Officer's facial expression and tone conveys interest
Notes: 1=Absent - facial expression and tone clearly conveyed LACK of interest throughout the scenario; 2=Limited - officer's facial expression and tone conveyed a limited level of interest, or any level of interest for less than half of the encounter; 3=Satisfactory - officer's expression and tone conveyed an appropriate level of interest for most of the encounter; 4=Exemplary - officer's expression and tone conveyed truly genuine/exemplary interest in the subject throughout the scenario.

ElementDescription: Q7 Officer used short, simple, and clear instructions, statements or questions.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer did not demonstrate this skill at all-and may have utilized lengthy multipronged questions/statements, or peppered the subject with rapid fire questions or instructions; 2=Limited - officer demonstrated this skill at some point during the scenario but not consistently; 3=Satisfactory - officer generally demonstrated this skill throughout the scenario; 4=Exemplary - officer expertly used short simple and clear instructions, statements, questions throughout the scenario.

ElementDescription: Q8 Officer used a sarcastic or condescending tone
Notes: 4=Never - officer was not sarcastic or condescending at all; 3=Limited - officer was mildly dismissive or condescending at some point during the scenario, but was not sarcastic or condescending during most of the encounter; 2=Mostly - officer's tone was moderately sarcastic and condescending for most of the scenario, or highly sarcastic and condescending for at least part of the scenario.

ElementDescription: Q9 Officer asked open-ended questions.
Notes: 1=Absent - no use of open-ended questions beyond initial approach; 2=Limited - officer made very limited use of open-ended questions (at least one beyond initial approach questions) but missed other opportunities; 3=Satisfactory - officer used open-ended questions appropriately throughout the encounter; 4=Exemplary - officer demonstrated exemplary use of open-ended questions.

ElementDescription: Q10 Officer used effective pauses.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer did not use any effective pauses; 2=Limited - officer demonstrated at least one effective pause, but missed most opportunities to do so; 3=Satisfactory - appropriate use of effective pauses; 4=Exemplary - use of effective pauses.

ElementDescription: Q11 Officer sought clarification of meaning, asked follow-up questions.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer did not seek clarification or ask any follow-up questions; 2=Limited - officer made a limited attempt to seek clarification or ask follow-up questions and missed many opportunities to do so; 3=Satisfactory - officer asked appropriate follow-up questions; 4=Exemplary - officer demonstrated exemplary use of follow-up/clarifying questions.

ElementDescription: Q12 Officer used summarizing or paraphrasing statements.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer did not use summarizing or paraphrasing statements at all; 2=Limited attempt to summarize or paraphrase and missed opportunities to use this skill; 3=Satisfactory - officer used summarizing or paraphrasing statements as appropriate; 4=Exemplary - officer very skillfully employed summarizing or paraphrasing statements to effectively convey understanding.

ElementDescription: Q13 Officer repeatedly made a command or asked a question the exact same way without trying to ask it differently or trying something else if a command is not followed.
Notes: 4=Never - officer did not do this at all; 3=Limited - officer did this at some point but shifted to more appropriate approach; 2=Mostly - officer did this for most the scenario; 1=Entirely - officer did this for the entire scenario.

ElementDescription: Q14 Officer labeled emotions.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer did not do this at all; 2=Limited - officer tried to do this at least once but missed opportunities or did this awkwardly; 3=Satisfactory - officer demonstrated appropriate use of this skill - labeling emotions in a sensitive manner at appropriate times; 4=Exemplary - officer demonstrated exemplary skill in labeling emotions (quality and quantity).

ElementDescription: Q15 Officer used reflective statements.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer did not do this at all; 2=Limited - officer demonstrated very limited use of reflective statements-perhaps awkwardly tried to use one; 4=Exemplary-officer demonstrated exemplary use of reflective statements (quality and quantity)

ElementDescription: Q16 Officer used minimal encouragers.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer did not use any minimal encouragers; 2=Limited/Emerging - officer used minimal encouragers at some point during the interaction-but missed opportunities to demonstrate they were actively engaged in the conversation.

ElementDescription: Q17 Officer asked questions at an inappropriate time or in an offensive tone.
Notes: 4=Never - officer only asked appropriately timed and toned questions; 3=Somewhat - officer asked an inappropriate question or did not time a question appropriately. This impacted rapport but officer shifted to more sensitive approach; 2=Mostly - officer was offensive most of the time and it significantly impacted rapport with the subject; 1=Entirely - officer used an offensive tone for the entire interaction.

ElementDescription: Q18 Officer asked appropriate mental health questions or questions that indicated recognition that the subject was experiencing a mental health problem.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer did not ask any mental health questions or asked in a highly insensitive way; 2=Limited - officer asked mental health related questions but in somewhat insensitive or awkward way; 3=Satisfactory - officer asked appropriate mental health questions sensitively; 4=Exemplary - officer very skillfully asked appropriate mental health questions.

ElementDescription: Q19 Officer used commands more than requests.
Notes: 1=Officer only used commands; 2=Commands were predominant; 3=Requests were predominant; 4=Officer only used requests.

ElementDescription: Q20 Officer was patient.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer was rushed and not listening to subject for entire interaction; 2=Limited/Emerging - officer demonstrated a limited amount of patience--but was rushed or impatient for some of the interaction; 3=Satisfactory - officer was generally patient and attentive to the subject throughout the interaction; 4=Exemplary - the officer demonstrated a high level of patience- slowed things down and listened to what the subject had to say.

ElementDescription: Q21 Officer gave subject enough time to do what was asked or to respond to questions.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer peppered the person with questions and/or commands without giving time to respond; 2=Limited/Emerging - officer may ''pepper'' commands or questions during most of the scenario, but at some point, tried to give subject more time to respond; 3=Satisfactory - officer generally gives the subject time to respond before asking another question or issuing a command; 4=Exemplary - officer does an exemplary job slowing things down and giving subject time to respond.

ElementDescription: Q22 Officer was interested in subject's concerns or issues.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer showed no signs of interest in the subject's concerns or issues; 2=Limited - officer demonstrated some interest but perhaps did not convey genuine interest; 3=Satisfactory - officer generally conveyed genuine interest; 4=Exemplary - officer does an exemplary job conveying genuine interest.

ElementDescription: Q23 Officer attempted to build rapport.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer made no effort to build rapport; 2=Limited - officer made limited effort/ineffective effort to build rapport; 3=Satisfactory - officer made appropriate effort to build rapport with the subject; 4=Exemplary - officer demonstrated exemplary and effective ability to build rapport.

ElementDescription: Q24 Officer fixated on a quick resolution to the reason for their interaction.
Notes: 4=Never - officer was not at all focused on a quick resolution; 3=Somewhat - officer was somewhat focused on getting to a quick resolution, but spent time talking with the person and trying to understand what was going on; 2=Mostly - officer was generally focused on a quick resolution, but made some limited effort to talk to the person about what was going on; 1=Entirely - officer was only focused on a quick resolution and made no effort to talk to the person about what was going on.

ElementDescription: Q25 Officer expressed empathy by making an effort to identify with the subject.
Notes: 1=Absent - officer made no attempt to express empathy or relate to the subject's situation; 2=Limited - officer made a limited attempt to express empathy/relate to the subject's situation, though perhaps not fully genuine; 3=Satisfactory - officer expressed empathy and appeared genuine; 4=Exemplary - officer very effectively expressed genuine empathy and connected with the subject's emotional experience.

ElementDescription: Q37 FOR PSYCHOSIS ONLY: Officer appropriately addressed the subject's delusions (did not argue, or pretend to buy, but acknowledged the person's experience) or subject's hallucinations.

Officer did not pretend to hear or buy-in, but acknowledged what subject was experiencing; 4=Exemplary - officer showed exemplary skill in addressing subject's delusions/hallucinations.
